name: Lex Walton
label: Sub Pop
lede: Lex Walton wrote a pop manifesto on the night shift as a security guard at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts, self-released a catalog that Sub Pop counts at a dozen or so records and Album of the Year counts at 36, and ended up on Sub Pop with Wolf Parade's Dan Boeckner producing.

eras.title: Youth Against Satan, a label of one
eras.text: Walton, then releasing as Alex, posted home-recorded albums, EPs and singles on Bandcamp under her own label, Youth Against Satan, and ran a blog of the same name.

years.src: Album of the Year: Lex Walton · Sub Pop: Sub Pop Signs Lex Walton · Vic Ramv: Lex Walton is Not Famous
years.h: Her own label, Youth Against Satan, starts putting out Walton's records
years.p: Album of the Year counts 36 releases since 2018, from singles to a live album. The label's look is deliberately chaotic, like a bootleg streaming site.
years.xp:
The 36 figure comes from Album of the Year's tally of 7 LPs, 5 EPs, 19 singles, 3 compilations, a demo and a live album, and it includes the SHAME MUSIC album listed for 2020. Sub Pop's own bio is more modest, calling it a dozen or so mostly home-recorded albums, EPs and singles.

Vic Ramv, writing about her, notes she makes her own music videos and cover art with basic tools like OSX Preview and iMovie.

eras.title: The Sound Rocker's Prayer
eras.text: In 2023 she posted her manifesto, opened for Ezra Furman in Somerville and released a 23-track album, describing her songs as plain reports of what had happened to her.

years.src: youthagainstsatan blog · Sub Pop: Sub Pop Signs Lex Walton
years.h: "The Sound Rocker's Prayer" goes up on her blog
years.p: [[Lex Walton|b6799f5e-77dc-456a-b456-9177b92b195c]] wrote the pop-music manifesto while working nights as a security guard at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston. Sub Pop still cites it in her bio.
years.xp: According to her blog, the post went up in September 2023 and was updated with an addendum on April 13, 2026. The later note describes a turn from aesthetic detachment toward what she calls direction, anger and love.

years.cap: Alex Walton with Ezra Furman outside The Sinclair in Cambridge.
years.src: WHRB: Becoming and Unbecoming With Alex Walton · Bandcamp: WOULD YOU KILL HER FOR $1,000,000???? · Northern Transmissions: Ezra Furman and Alex Walton · YouTube: Ezra Furman and Alex Walton
yt: Ezra Furman and Alex Walton, Tie Me To The Train Tracks (live at the Rockwell)
years.h: Walton opens for Ezra Furman at The Rockwell in Somerville
years.p: She was 23 and still billing herself as Alex Walton. Harvard's WHRB interviewed her about the show.
years.xp:
Journey Whitney's interview ran October 18, 2023. Walton said she had lost any ability for metaphor or storytelling and now just relayed events from her life, and that the goal was making people feel less alone. She also said her transness is part of the work and that she wants younger queer fans at her shows to see someone like themselves.

The two played a duet of "Tie Me To The Train Tracks" at the Rockwell date. Furman and Walton released it as a single on October 27, 2024, and Furman said they made it at Walton's old house in Roxbury, Boston, in a burst of neurotic passion.

Her EP WOULD YOU KILL HER FOR $1,000,000????, credited to Alex Walton, followed on October 17 as a preview of the album.

years.src: Bandcamp: I WANT YOU TO KILL ME · WHRB: Becoming and Unbecoming With Alex Walton · Album of the Year: Lex Walton
years.h: I WANT YOU TO KILL ME runs 23 tracks and 70 minutes
years.p: Walton released it as Alex Walton on Bandcamp, calling it a vessel for "the worst year of my life."
years.xp:
Her own description lists almost dying, idiosyncratic ex-lovers and recovering from almost dying among the subjects, and says every word is from life. It was first titled Hyperconfessional and Overwhelmingly Sincere, per WHRB.

Album of the Year has no critic reviews for it, but users ranked it 89th among 2023's highest-rated albums there.

eras.title: Demos for sale, a five-hour film
eras.text: Walton put out eight demos with a plea to buy them, and played Circle in a five-hour film shot on Hi8.

years.src: Bandcamp: SHAMELESS DESPERATE CASHGRAB FOR BAD TIMES
years.h: Eight demos, a cashgrab in the title, a plea to buy
years.p: SHAMELESS DESPERATE CASHGRAB FOR BAD TIMES collects demos "of varying quality from the last year or so." The Bandcamp page asks listeners to buy if they can.
years.xp: The Bandcamp note reads: "my health is not good. please buy if you can. theyre good songs i promise." Track titles include "Covered In Angels" and "Dashcam Confessional."

years.src: Wikipedia: Castration Movie · Screen Slate: Castration Movie Anthology II · Sub Pop: Sub Pop Signs Lex Walton
years.h: Walton plays Circle, a restless cult member, in a five-hour Hi8 movie
years.p: Louise Weard's Castration Movie Anthology II: The Best of Both Worlds puts [[Lex Walton|b6799f5e-77dc-456a-b456-9177b92b195c]] in the lead, in a basement.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia the film ran about 300 minutes and, like the first Anthology, was shot on a Hi8 camcorder, one take per scene, with crew handed the camera with minimal experience. Screen Slate called it a warts-and-all effort of maximalism.

Sub Pop lists the role in her bio. Wikipedia's page shows the credit as Lex Walton in the cast list.

eras.title: Sub Pop signs her, Boeckner produces
eras.text: In August 2026 Sub Pop signed Walton worldwide and released a seven-song record produced with Dan Boeckner. Pitchfork gave it an 8.3.

years.src: Sub Pop: Sub Pop Signs Lex Walton · Sub Pop: Watch Lex Walton's New Official Video
years.h: Sub Pop signs Walton and releases her first record for the label the same day
years.p: The label took her on worldwide for 2026 and beyond, and put the seven songs of ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER on streaming.
years.xp:
Sub Pop's bio calls her a NYC-based songwriter, actress, prose poet and filmmaker with an approach of unflinching confessionality, and says she has collaborated with Devi McCallion of Black Dresses, Geese and Ezra Furman.

The label held a Bandcamp listening party the same day. CD and Opaque Blue vinyl follow November 20 in North America and January 22, 2027 in the EU and UK.

years.src: Sub Pop: ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER · The Fire Note: Lex Walton, ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER · Wikipedia: Dan Boeckner
years.h: ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER runs seven songs, about 20 minutes
years.p: [[Dan Boeckner|142c1d98-df0e-4df5-b202-e63814693024]] co-produced and [[Ben Greenberg|87045e8c-9f93-4444-9d7e-b21bfd3836f5]] recorded it at Thump and Circular Ruin in Williamsburg.
years.xp:
Guests: Sarah Neufeld of Arcade Fire, Emily Green and Sam Revaz of Geese, and Greenberg of Uniform and the Men. Boeckner, of Wolf Parade and Handsome Furs, has been on Sub Pop since Wolf Parade signed there.

The Fire Note described lean, scruffy garage rock with indie post-punk cool. Paste, quoted by Sub Pop, called it "wiggly, anxious power pop."

years.src: Sub Pop: News from 8/2026 · The Fat Angel Sings: Lex Walton, Hipster Runoff · YouTube: Lex Walton, Hipster Runoff (Official Music Video)
years.h: "Hipster Runoff" opens the record by naming names
years.p: The lead single takes on Ariel Pink, Wavves, Kony 2012 and the algorithm, with strings by [[Sarah Neufeld|3ef8c35a-bc9f-49e4-b17d-2df4238696c0]].
years.xp: Sub Pop lists the song as the lead single. Walton told the label she wanted to capture "the lifespan of the blogosphere buzzband aughts-rocker with all of its triumphs and valleys."

years.src: Sub Pop: Watch Lex Walton's New Official Video
yt: Adrian Borland Will Have His Revenge On London (video)
years.h: She shot the "Adrian Borland" video the day after her apartment burned
years.p: Lev Heftler co-directed the video for "Adrian Borland Will Have His Revenge On London."
years.xp: Walton says: "Filmed by me and Lev Heftler the day after my apartment burned down as we day drank and stumbled through the wreckage."

years.big: Earnest and disaffected, ironic and confrontational
q: Earnest and disaffected, ironic and confrontational
years.src: Album of the Year: ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER · The Fire Note: Lex Walton, ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER
years.p: [[Hannah Jocelyn|4bbcae94-4a7d-4cb3-b7fd-533512ed03fd]]'s review calls Walton a Brooklyn artist channeling trans rage into scrappy DIY punk.
years.xp: Album of the Year, which lists the Pitchfork review as 83, notes that some listeners wanted more than roughly 19 minutes. The record ends on "Ultimate Love 4Ever."

years.src: Sub Pop: Watch Lex Walton's New Official Video · Sub Pop: ULTIMATE LOVE FOREVER
years.h: Sub Pop puts her on the Showbox bill with her producer's band
years.p: She opens for [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]], Boeckner's band, at the Showbox at the Market in Seattle.
years.xp: Announced dates before that: Webster Hall in New York on September 30 with Frog, and Prospect Park on October 10 with the Format.
